decisions.evidenceText: It does not explain the existence of evil because knowledge of that already existed before she committed the fall.
decisions.rationale: The positive attribution-error rule applies because the response explicitly says the fall is wrongly credited with explaining something that already existed. The default would be no diagnostic defect without an explicit defect cue, but “does not explain” supplies one; invalid-inference is excluded because no defective inference step is identified.

decisions.evidenceText: Well, I went from Christianity to Islam.
decisions.rationale: The positive exact-proposition rule is not met: this reverse-conversion example does not affirm, deny, or otherwise state the component about Koukl’s former-Muslim acquaintances and their reported satisfaction. The default is no contact absent explicit propositional contact, and exact-proposition is excluded rather than inferred from topical similarity.

decisions.evidenceText: there's people that would have gone the other way
decisions.rationale: The positive exact-proposition rule applies because the expressly opposite conversion cases directly challenge the claimed evidentiary force of one-way changed lives against interchangeability. The default would be none without propositional contact, but “the other way” explicitly connects the countercases; none is therefore excluded.

decisions.evidenceText: they'll be in the comment section right now saying, "Well, I went from Christianity to Islam."
decisions.rationale: The positive classification rule requires component-contact-precludes-contrary whenever any target component has positive contact, and the reverse-conversion example positively contacts the second component’s evidentiary claim. The default relevant-no-component classification applies only when every component lacks contact, so it is excluded here.
